title: The Agent Role Contract
summary: A browser-local, downloadable eighteen-field contract for defining an AI agent’s mission, scope, permissions, evidence rules, approvals, escalation, logging, evaluation, failure response, and accountable human owner.
audience: Leaders, operators, and builders turning a named AI agent into a bounded and governable organizational role.
implementationStatus: Public browser-local form with Markdown preview and download; no entered information is transmitted or stored.
documentation: Download the completed or blank contract as Markdown
Have the accountable owner approve and maintain it

fields.label: Agent name
fields.hint: The recognizable name; optional because the contract, not the name, is the point.

fields.label: Role
fields.hint: The one job this agent holds.

fields.label: Mission
fields.placeholder: e.g. Keep every published output on-brand and consistent.

fields.label: Scope
fields.placeholder: e.g. Review drafts for voice, clarity, and consistency; suggest edits.

fields.label: Inputs
fields.placeholder: e.g. Draft text and the brand voice guide.

fields.label: Data classification
fields.placeholder: e.g. Internal — no personal or regulated data.

fields.label: Tools
fields.placeholder: e.g. The draft document only. No email, no publishing.

fields.label: Prohibited actions
fields.hint: What it may never do. Be specific.
fields.placeholder: e.g. Never send, publish, post, spend, or contact anyone.

fields.label: Output format
fields.hint: The shape of what it returns.
fields.placeholder: e.g. Marked-up draft plus a short list of flags.

fields.label: Evidence rule
fields.hint: What sources or support it must show.
fields.placeholder: e.g. Cite the guideline behind each flag.

fields.label: Confidence rule
fields.hint: When it must say it is unsure.
fields.placeholder: e.g. Flag, do not guess, when a call is subjective.

fields.label: Human approval
fields.placeholder: e.g. Any publish decision routes to the owner.

fields.label: Escalation
fields.placeholder: e.g. Any legal, medical, or financial claim escalates.

fields.label: Logging
fields.placeholder: e.g. Every review and flag, with timestamp.

fields.label: Evaluation
fields.placeholder: e.g. Sampled monthly against the voice guide.

fields.label: Failure response
fields.hint: What happens when the agent breaks.
fields.placeholder: e.g. Stop the workflow and notify the owner.

fields.label: Owner
fields.hint: The accountable human; always a person.

evidence: The intended business role and representative tasks
Applicable data, tool, approval, retention, and escalation requirements
Named human ownership and evaluation records
methodology: Define one bounded role
Specify permitted inputs, tools, and outputs
Prohibit consequential autonomous actions
Attach evidence, confidence, approval, and escalation rules
Assign logging, retention, evaluation, failure response, and a human owner
assumptions: The organization will test the contract against representative work
Permissions and technical controls will enforce the written boundaries
limitations: A written role contract does not itself enforce permissions or establish compliance
Qualified legal, privacy, security, and domain review may still be required

title: Continuing education built to the same standard as everything else here.
summary: Evidence-based, primary-source continuing education in artificial intelligence, neuroscience, ethics, psychedelic care, and emerging professional practice for counselors, social workers, psychologists, healthcare providers, attorneys, and other practitioners.
audience: Practitioners and institutions seeking rigorous cross-disciplinary education with explicit evidence, learning, ethics, and quality-assurance standards.
architecture: Eight-course AI CE launch series totaling fourteen planned hours
Three-course psychedelic and neuroscience launch series totaling nine planned hours
Twelve additional series developed as accreditation and demand justify
Timed agendas, measurable learning outcomes, evaluation forms, and profession-specific credit pathways
implementationStatus: Course content is being developed for submission; provider accreditation and co-sponsorship are in progress. Credit is not represented as available until the applicable approval is confirmed.
documentation: Primary-source citations verified against original authority
Timed agenda and measurable learning outcomes per course
Evaluation instrument and profession-specific ethics alignment
roadmap: Prioritize NBCC, NASW, and NAADAC pathways
Confirm licensed co-presenters where professional-credit rules require them
Publish credit status separately for each course and board
Expand into healthcare, law, governance, research literacy, pedagogy, and emerging-therapy series
changelog: 2026 launch catalog: eight AI courses and three psychedelic/neuroscience courses identified
Accreditation targets disclosed as targets rather than awarded credit
licensing: Institutional delivery, accredited-provider partnerships, co-sponsorship, and curriculum licensing are scoped only after the applicable approval, presenter, attribution, and quality-control terms are confirmed.
evidence: Primary scientific, legal, regulatory, ethical, and professional sources
Learning objectives, timed agendas, assessments, and evaluation records
methodology: Define the practitioner and measurable learning outcome
Build from primary and authoritative sources
Audit claims and citations across four correction cycles
Align ethics content to the applicable professional standards
Confirm accreditation before representing credit as available
assumptions: Accreditation and co-sponsorship requirements will be verified for each audience and jurisdiction
Qualified presenters and reviewers will be engaged where required
limitations: Accreditation is in progress and no unconfirmed credit is promised
Educational content is not legal, medical, clinical, tax, or other professional advice

title: How your audience trusts you is a mechanism, not a mood board.
summary: A neuroscience-informed audience-perception audit that maps processing fluency, mere exposure, source credibility, and affect to a prioritized trust architecture and governed AI content-operations plan.
audience: Agency leaders, CMOs, founders, and creative directors who own brand perception and must defend the decisions used to shape it.
timeline: A scoped engagement begins with representative brand assets, audience and category context, then moves through perception audit, trust architecture, and content-system design.
fit: The brand is unfamiliar or inconsistently expressed
Creative direction needs a defensible mechanism rather than generic adjectives
Claims and proof are not sequenced to the audience’s familiarity
Content operations must compound recognition without losing voice or review

fields.label: Current friction signals
fields.hint: Select every signal that is true.

bands.title: Strong footing
bands.summary: The foundations are visible; concentrate on evidence, disciplined repetition, and category-specific testing.

bands.title: Mixed footing
bands.summary: The brand has usable signals but material fluency, familiarity, affect, or credibility gaps remain.

bands.title: Foundational work first
bands.summary: Reduce processing friction and establish a consistent signal before asking the audience to absorb larger claims.

recommendations.text: Reduce visual and verbal processing effort: one clear claim, stronger hierarchy, and higher figure-ground contrast.
Repeat a stable set of recognizable cues before introducing more concepts or changing the system.
Use specific, verifiable proof and named expertise; do not substitute louder claims for evidence.
Make the intended feeling explicit and test whether aesthetic and language choices consistently produce it.

evidence: Representative brand assets, audience context, category conventions, and performance signals
Published cognitive mechanisms including processing fluency, mere exposure, source credibility, and affect
Dated and confidence-rated source record for material claims
methodology: Build a research and intelligence layer from the brand, category, and audience
Map observed friction to named cognitive mechanisms
Resolve the findings into a prioritized operator decision layer
Design a governed editorial distribution and signal architecture
Refresh inputs and review outcomes without claiming guaranteed lift
assumptions: The engagement receives representative assets and audience context
Mechanism-level findings are tested against the actual category and population
limitations: The public diagnostic is illustrative and not a validated psychometric instrument
Cognitive mechanisms do not guarantee a fixed commercial outcome and effect sizes vary by context

title: Institutions shape how people think, trust, and decide.
summary: A research-and-advisory practice for nervous-system-aware institutional design and governance, using a fourteen-dimension framework across legal, healthcare, technology, civic, built-environment, and extreme-environment systems.
audience: Institutions and leaders designing rules, spaces, technologies, communications, and procedures where stress, uncertainty, trust, adoption, and legitimacy matter.
architecture: Fifteen domain modules spanning legal and justice, healthcare and clinical, civic and built environment, education, work, spaceflight, and confined settings
A shared human-adoption lens with Aloha AI but a distinct advisory storefront and buyer
implementationStatus: Public research framework and advisory orientation. Domain application requires additional evidence, stakeholders, and qualified professional review.
roadmap: Publish the full framework and module documentation
Operationalize measures and evidence standards by domain
Develop advisory pilots with accountable institutional partners
Evaluate whether changes improve comprehension, trust, participation, and safe adoption
changelog: 2026 public orientation defines the fourteen-dimension, fifteen-module architecture and the boundary between NSAG and Aloha AI
licensing: Advisory, institutional research, framework adaptation, and licensing require an explicit scope, professional responsibilities, evidence standards, ownership, and evaluation terms.
evidence: Neuroscience, psychology, human-factors, design, governance, and domain-specific evidence
Observed institutional workflows, spaces, communications, and behavior
Stakeholder experience and accountable professional judgment
methodology: Identify where the institution asks stressed or uncertain people to understand, trust, or act
Map threat, ambiguity, agency, predictability, belonging, and cognitive-load conditions
Redesign the space, rule, process, communication, or tool
Keep licensed and accountable judgment attached
Evaluate comprehension, participation, trust, harm, and unintended effects
assumptions: Institutions will include affected stakeholders and accountable domain professionals
The framework will be adapted rather than treated as a universal causal model
limitations: NSAG is a governance framework and method, not legal, medical, financial, clinical, or tax advice
Nervous-system-aware design does not erase structural power, resource, legal, or implementation constraints
